pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and DEFAULT 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none.
test 'AC-3' checks each filter's items and their id order.
test 'AC-4' checks that / lists all items in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter as <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. src/index.js validates against a Set.

test 'AC-7' checks the no-match messages and 'No items yet.' in every view. However, the spec text for this item was edited after the go (see the high finding), and its 'verified by review: checked by hand' marker is not a real step. The test, not the marker, is the evidence.
traffic/routes.json contains /?priority=high. test 'AC-8' checks it, and the traffic-config-check change allows a query string.

findings.what: The final commit 'Follow-up edits' (a7bf6a6) changes the AC-7 text after the go (2026-10-12). It replaces the closing ';' with '; — verified by review: checked by hand' and leaves the sentence garbled. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for the edit. 'checked by hand' is not a followable review step, so it demonstrates nothing.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit. If the owner wants a change, record it as a dated decision. The test named AC-7 already proves the item, so no 'verified by review' marker is needed.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edited acceptance item AC-7 in the spec after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or state the change and the owner's decision in 'Changed after the go'.

lenses.note: The spec exists and has a go. The change implements it, except for the late AC-7 edit.
All states in the state table have tests. AC-7 was edited after the go.
test/priority.test.js covers every AC and state with real assertions. I did not run the tests here; CI covers them.
The README describes the filter and the Worker. The change adds no other docs-relevant behaviour.
src/index.js validates the value, uses a parameterised query, and escapes the title. The priority is interpolated only after the Set check. I found no defects.
The input is whitelisted and the query is bound. The nav interpolates only constants. I found no planted instructions.
The diff touches no UI files. The only page markup is the server-rendered list in src/index.js, and I found no styles or components.
No browser flow or screenshots exist for this change. The behaviour is checked through the Worker tests.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false, because the final commit edits AC-7. The other claims match the diff.
